Definition: adverb from a derivative of G3071; Lycaonistically, i.e. in the language of the Lycaonians:--in the speech of Lycaonia.
BiblicalUsage: The word is an adverb meaning in the language of Lycaonia, and it appears once, when the crowds at Lystra saw Paul heal the lame man and lifted up their voices in the speech of Lycaonia, saying the gods had come down to them in the likeness of men.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the crowd's own tongue betrayed them: they cried out in Lycaonian because the miracle had struck them where they lived, and yet they still missed who had done it.
